unit.title: Two Suitcases and Nowhere to Sleep

station-dusk.description: Evening train station with warm windows

station-night.description: Night café scene with warm window light

content.narration:
You step out of the station.
Two suitcases. One backpack.
Your phone shows 11% battery.
content.thought: Okay. New city. No place to sleep tonight.

messages: Hey! I'm so sorry I can't pick you up — my seminar ran late. Are you at the station?

dialogue.speaker: Priya — voice message
dialogue.text: Hey! I'm so sorry I can't pick you up — my seminar ran late. Are you at the station?

content.narration: You look at the screen and start typing…

email.subject: Accommodation Update
email.body:
Dear Student,

We are sorry to inform you that your accommodation has been cancelled.

The landlord no longer accepts international students at this property.

You may need to find your own place.

Best regards,
Oakfield Housing Agency

content.narration: You open your email and read the letter from your housing agency again.
content.thought: Cancelled? They took my deposit last month…

messages: Okay, don't panic. This happens sometimes. But do you know anything about renting a flat here?

dialogue.speaker: Priya
dialogue.text: Wait — they did WHAT? Okay, don't panic. But first — do you know anything about renting a flat here?

question.label: Quick check
question.text: What is your situation right now?

options.text: I have a place tonight, find one tomorrow
No place tonight — I need to find one now
I can get a refund and stay in a hotel

question.feedback: Right. No place to sleep tonight. Let's find you a flat. Fast.

listings.desc: Spacious 1-bed flat, furnished. All bills included.

content.narration: You open a rental website. The page loads. Dozens of listings appear. But the words are all… different.
content.thought: Every word looks simple. But together they don't make sense.

messages: Test yourself! If you want your own space with kitchen and bathroom, which do you pick?

dialogue.speaker: Priya
dialogue.text: Test yourself! If you want your own space with kitchen and bathroom, which do you pick?

quiz.question: You want a private home on one floor with its own kitchen and bathroom. You search for a:
quiz.label: Vocabulary

options.text: Flat — your own home on one floor

quiz.feedback: Right! A flat is a full home on one floor — separate rooms, private kitchen and bathroom. A studio has everything in one room.

listings.desc: Spacious 1-bed flat, furnished. Bed, desk, wardrobe included. All bills included.
Cosy studio, unfurnished. Empty room. Deposit required.

slides.thoughtBubble:
Spacious… furnished… so that one has everything.

But 'cosy' and 'unfurnished' — smaller, and empty. I'd need to buy a bed, a desk…

content.narration: Three results show up on your screen. You read the descriptions carefully.
content.thought:
Spacious… furnished… so that one has everything already.

But 'cosy' and 'unfurnished' — smaller, and empty.

messages: Don't just scroll! Do you know what these words really mean?

dialogue.speaker: Priya
dialogue.text: Don't just scroll! Do you know what these words really mean?

quiz.question: "Furnished" means:
quiz.label: Question 1

options.text: Has furniture — you can move in right away

quiz.feedback: Yes! Furnished = bed, desk, wardrobe included.

quiz.question: "Cosy" in a rental ad usually means:
quiz.label: Question 2

options.text: Small — a nice way of saying "tiny"

quiz.feedback: Right! In UK ads, "cosy" ≈ small. Not bad — just honest to know.

messages: The bedsit is cheap for a reason.
'En-suite bathroom' = at least your bathroom is private. That's something.

dialogue.speaker: Priya
dialogue.text: The bedsit is cheap for a reason. 'Shared kitchen' = you cook with strangers. 'En-suite bathroom' = at least your bathroom is private. That's something.

content.narration: You look at the price again. 380 per month.
content.thought:
Shared kitchen with strangers… I've heard stories.
But the price…

content.decisionText: Which flat do you call about?
content.narration: Each choice leads to a different story. There's no perfect answer.

decisions.title: Spacious Flat
decisions.desc: Furnished — has bed, desk, wardrobe. All bills included.
decisions.feedback: You call about the flat. It sounds easy — everything's included. But your budget is tight…

decisions.title: Cosy Studio
decisions.desc: Unfurnished — empty. You buy your own furniture.
decisions.feedback: You call about the studio. It's empty but affordable. Tomorrow you can go to IKEA.

decisions.title: Bedsit
decisions.desc: Shared kitchen. En-suite bathroom. No guarantor needed.
decisions.feedback: You call about the bedsit. It's cheap — very cheap. But you'll share a kitchen with strangers…

dialogue.speaker: Agent
dialogue.text: Yes, the studio is still available. It's five twenty per calendar month.

dialogue.speaker: Agent
dialogue.text: Each month. And we require a deposit of five twenty as well.

dialogue.speaker: Agent on the phone
dialogue.text: It's five twenty per calendar month… And we require a deposit of five twenty as well.

content.narration: You hang up and open your phone's calculator.
content.thought: 520 + 520… that's over a thousand pounds for the first month.

question.label: Budget check
question.text: Rent: £520 + Deposit: £520 + Basic furniture: ~£300. Your balance is £1,840. Do you have enough?

options.text: Yes — enough, with some left over

question.feedback: Correct! £1,840 − £1,340 = £500 left. Tight, but enough to start. You need to move fast.

dialogues.speaker: Agent
dialogues.text: We'll need one more thing — a UK guarantor. Someone who promises to pay if you can't.

dialogues.speaker: You
dialogues.text: I… don't know anyone in the UK.

dialogues.speaker: Agent
dialogues.text: Then I'm sorry, we can't proceed.

content.thought: A guarantor. Of course. I just moved here yesterday.

messages: Guarantor problem? Yeah, that's the number one issue for international students. But there are solutions.
Your university might offer a guarantor service. Or you can pay a few months upfront.

dialogue.speaker: Priya (calling you back)
dialogue.text: Guarantor problem? Yeah, that's the number one issue. But your university might offer a guarantor service. Or you can pay a few months upfront.

content.narration: All three are real solutions. But which one makes the most sense for you?

decisions.title: Go to the university tomorrow
decisions.desc: Ask about their guarantor service for international students

decisions.title: Pay three months upfront
decisions.desc: Save £200 but spend a big chunk of your savings

decisions.title: Find a flat that doesn't need a guarantor
decisions.desc: Like that bedsit — but is it worth the risk?

content.narration:
It's fully dark now.
You find a café and order a coffee.
It's 3.80.
content.thought:
Two suitcases. No flat yet.
But I know more than I did an hour ago.

messages: Hey, you're doing fine. First day is always the worst. Here's what you learned today:
Sleep well. Tomorrow we go to the university office.

dialogue.speaker: Priya
dialogue.text: Hey, you're doing fine. First day is always the worst. Here's what you learned today — you'll need all of it:

quizTF.statement: "Deposit" is money you get back when you leave.
"PCM" means the price for one month.
A "studio" has a separate kitchen and bathroom.

timeline.text: You arrived — two suitcases, no plan
Agency cancelled — your room was gone
Learned the words — flat, studio, bedsit, furnished, unfurnished…
Called a flat — deposit + PCM = £1,040 for month one
Hit a wall — no guarantor, no flat
Survived day one — tomorrow you go to the university

content.recapSubtitle:
You arrived with nothing, found out your room was cancelled, learned a whole new vocabulary, got rejected by an agent, and ended up in a café at 3.80 coffee.

Tomorrow: the university office. But tonight — you survived.

unitCards.title: Unit 1 — "Two Suitcases and Nowhere to Sleep"
unitCards.desc: You learned to read rental listings, understand prices, and deal with the guarantor problem.

unitCards.title: Unit 2 — "The View That Wasn't What It Seemed"
unitCards.desc: You go to the university office for help — then visit your first flat in person. The photos were… misleading.

unitCards.title: Unit 3 — "Mrs. Fletcher's Fine Print"
unitCards.desc: The contract arrives. It's 12 pages long. Every word looks important. Which ones actually are?

content.nextDesc: You visit your first flat. The photos showed a bright, spacious room. The real thing has a window facing a brick wall and a landlord who says "it gets darker in winter."

slides.storySummary: Arrived → Agency cancelled → Learned the words → Found options → Hit the guarantor wall → Survived day one
